items.title: Context Engineering (Agent Memory) for AI Agents Starts with Retrieval
items.summary_1line: Agents waste time and context on clumsy searches, oversized results and stale data. Learn the retrieval techniques LangChain's Deep Agents harness uses to get the right context in.
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, harness, eval.
items.editor_note: Practitioner angle: LangChain describes retrieval techniques its Deep Agents harness uses against clumsy searches, oversized results, and stale data.

editorial.tldr: From Oct 3 to Oct 17, papers examined retrieval in agents and on-device LLMs under execution constraints: CPU retrieval scheduling, skill routing, tool retrieval, and agent memory. The shared thread was that retrieval is judged by what happens at run time, not only by semantic match.
editorial.whats_new: LangChain's Oct 23 post says its Deep Agents harness fixes clumsy searches, oversized results, and stale data to get the right context in, moving the theme from papers to a shipped harness.
editorial.why_it_matters: Retrieval for skills, tools, and memory can fail at run time through unavailable tools, latency contention, oversized results, or stale data, so relevance-only scoring is not enough.
editorial.take_for_builders: Log for each retrieved tool, skill, or memory whether it was available and succeeded at run time, and cap result size, so you can measure the gap these papers and LangChain's post target.

status.detail: Four papers frame retrieval as an execution problem; LangChain's Oct 23 post is the first practitioner write-up in the thread.
